decisions.reason: Although its separate web visibility disappeared by 2020-2021, it is still a core cardboard quarter-pallet variant tied to prior launch investment, so management would more likely continue than reverse course.
The pegboard-back display remains close to the established cardboard display business, and sunk development and range-extension logic support persistence despite weaker recent public visibility.
As the most standard quarter-pallet cardboard display in the firm's core offer, it is the easiest to justify keeping even if it is no longer individually highlighted.
This eighth-pallet format is a familiar extension of the main display line, so escalation of commitment and portfolio continuity still favor keeping it on the market.

Because this media-focused quarter-pallet display is narrower in application and no longer visibly promoted, management can more readily redirect resources while treating the withdrawal as portfolio refocusing rather than failure.
